research_question: How Much Purchase History Is Needed to Predict Future Customer Revenue? A Comparison of Simple and Machine Learning Models
source: Original Online Retail II workbook, two sheets, dates 2009-12-01 to 2011-12-09
status: experimental design frozen at Milestone 2; features/models not built
target: sum of positive quantity × positive unit price across known customer transactions for 30 calendar days [cutoff, cutoff+30); GBP; gross recorded sales, not net of refunds
population: customers with >=1 positive sale in [cutoff-90d, cutoff); all are evaluated at all history windows, even if 30d/60d inputs have zero purchases
features_to_generate_next_milestone: purchase recency capped to window+1 days when no purchases
split_logic: chronological by cutoff; last training label end <= first validation cutoff; last validation label end <= first test cutoff
baseline: gross historical spend × (30 / history_window_days), zero for no transactions within window
primary_metric: MAE (GBP) on untouched chronological test snapshots
secondary_metrics: RMSE and median absolute error for sensitivity to extreme buyers
top 10% predicted customer future revenue capture vs actual
fairness: identical eligible snapshots at all 3 history windows
shared target, test snapshots and feature definitions
same historical information horizon for all compared models
leakage_guards: per snapshot feature date < cutoff and feature date >= cutoff-W
no final test outcomes in feature fitting, tuning, scaling or feature selection
earlier outcome windows do not overlap subsequent split start
limitations: Repeated customer snapshots correlated; account for dependence in uncertainty
Dataset is 2009-2011 UK retail with wholesale characteristics, not modern DTC advertising
Returns/cancellations excluded, so prediction target is gross positive invoiced sales not net realized revenue
Extreme single-line and customer spending outliers will be disclosed; robustness tests of prediction errors on and excluding top-1%-revenue customers may be informative
Customer IDs missing on many rows; population restricted to identifiable customers
Historical purchasing of new customers / customer churn outside 90-day activity window not evaluated
disclosure: No ML fitting or trained results in Milestone 2
Source CSV records include customer IDs present in the public dataset; do not upload proprietary customer data
